answer: In a compute market, sonnet buys a comet simulation from zenith. Each paid job commits its inputs before a public random beacon selects hidden test cases. Rewards depend on correct outputs checked by independently sampled verifiers, not on votes from newly created accounts. Payment is capped by verified computation, and identical job commitments cannot be claimed twice. An attacker running 100 aliases must perform 100 distinct computations and pay their energy and hardware costs; copying identities creates no extra payable work.
